notes: All rates are GST-inclusive, in c/kWh (usage) and c/day (supply).
Reference prices are the regulated caps or standing offer prices. Most households are on market offers, which retailers set and which are often lower.
Windows are [start hour, end hour) in the time basis given for each network: 'local' follows daylight saving, 'AEST' does not.
Periods are matched in order; the first period whose window, months and days include the hour applies. A period with "rest": true covers every hour not matched by an earlier period.

dmo.name: Default Market Offer (DMO 8)
dmo.doc: Default market offer prices 2026-27: Final determination, May 2026, Appendix C
dmo.about: The DMO is the maximum price a retailer can charge households on a standing offer in New South Wales, South East Queensland and South Australia. From 2026-27 the AER also caps the daily supply charge and each usage rate. It is set by the Australian Energy Regulator each May and published at aer.gov.au.

sso.name: Solar Sharer Offer
sso.provider: Australian Government, with tariffs capped by the Australian Energy Regulator
sso.doc: Default market offer prices 2026-27: Final determination, May 2026, Appendix C (6)
sso.about: An opt-in plan, from 1 July 2026, with three free hours of electricity each day (11am to 2pm in New South Wales and South East Queensland, 12pm to 3pm in South Australia), up to 24 kWh a day. Retailers with more than 1,000 customers in DMO areas must offer it, and households need a smart meter. It was introduced by the Australian Government, and its tariffs are capped by the Australian Energy Regulator as part of the DMO, published at aer.gov.au.

vdo.name: Victorian Default Offer (VDO)
vdo.about: The VDO is the regulated price for Victorian households on standing offers. It is set by the Essential Services Commission each year and published at esc.vic.gov.au.

qca.name: Notified prices, regional Queensland
qca.doc: Queensland Government Gazette No. 29, 5 June 2026 (prices published exclusive of GST; GST added here)
qca.about: Notified prices are the regulated prices retailers must charge standard contract customers in regional Queensland (outside the Energex area). They are set by the Queensland Competition Authority each June and published at qca.org.au.

qca_fit.name: Regional Queensland feed-in tariff
qca_fit.about: The regulated rate paid for rooftop solar exported by eligible small customers in regional Queensland. It is set by the Queensland Competition Authority each June and published at qca.org.au.

icrc.name: ActewAGL standard plan (ICRC regulated)
icrc.provider: Independent Competition and Regulatory Commission (ICRC), ACT
icrc.doc: ACT Standard plan electricity prices, schedule of charges from 1 July 2026
icrc.about: The standing offer prices for ACT households, which are regulated by the Independent Competition and Regulatory Commission (icrc.act.gov.au) and published by ActewAGL.

otter.name: Aurora Energy standing offer (regulated)
otter.provider: Office of the Tasmanian Economic Regulator (OTTER)
otter.doc: Aurora Energy 2026-27 Standing Offer Tariff Schedule
otter.about: The standing offer prices for Tasmanian households, approved by the Office of the Tasmanian Economic Regulator (economicregulator.tas.gov.au) and published by Aurora Energy.

otter_fit.name: Tasmanian regulated feed-in tariff
otter_fit.provider: Office of the Tasmanian Economic Regulator (OTTER)
otter_fit.doc: Media release: regulated electricity prices and feed-in tariff rate for 2026-27
otter_fit.about: The minimum rate retailers must offer eligible Tasmanian customers for exported rooftop solar. It is set by the Office of the Tasmanian Economic Regulator and published at economicregulator.tas.gov.au.

ipart.name: IPART solar feed-in tariff benchmarks
ipart.provider: Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal (IPART), NSW
ipart.doc: All-day and time-of-day solar feed-in tariff benchmarks 2026-27
ipart.about: IPART's estimate of what exported rooftop solar is worth in New South Wales. It is a guide only: retailers can pay more, less or nothing. It is set by the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal and published at ipart.nsw.gov.au.

vic_fit.name: Victorian feed-in tariffs
vic_fit.doc: The ESC stopped setting a minimum feed-in tariff from 1 July 2025
vic_fit.about: Since 1 July 2025 Victorian retailers set their own feed-in tariffs, which cannot be below 0c/kWh. The Essential Services Commission (esc.vic.gov.au) no longer sets a minimum.

sa_fit.name: South Australian feed-in tariffs
sa_fit.doc: ESCOSA stopped setting a minimum retailer feed-in tariff from 1 January 2017
sa_fit.about: South Australian retailers set their own feed-in tariffs. The Essential Services Commission of South Australia (escosa.sa.gov.au) has not set a minimum since 2017.

ausgrid_export.name: Ausgrid two-way solar pricing
ausgrid_export.about: A network charge and credit for exported solar that Ausgrid applies to retailers, for customers who can export, since July 2025. Retailers decide how, or whether, it shows on a bill. Details are at ausgrid.com.au.

sapn_export.name: SA Power Networks export tariff
sapn_export.about: A network charge for exported solar that SA Power Networks applies to retailers. Retailers decide how, or whether, it shows on a bill. Details are at sapowernetworks.com.au.

export.applies: Applies to retailers for customers who can export, since July 2025

networks.name: Endeavour Energy
networks.area: Western Sydney, Blue Mountains, Southern Highlands and Illawarra

networks.name: Essential Energy
networks.area: Regional and rural New South Wales

export.applies: Applies to retailers for customers who export
